sumber: DSKP Bahasa Inggeris KSSR (Semakan 2017, CEFR) Year 3; unit themes of the Year 3 textbook

nota.t: Introducing yourself
Hi, I'm Hana. I'm nine years old. I'm from Malaysia. · How do you spell your name? — H-A-N-A.
Numbers 11–100
eleven · twelve · thirteen · fourteen · fifteen · twenty · thirty · forty · fifty · sixty · seventy · eighty · ninety · one hundred
thirteen (13) and thirty (30) sound alike. Listen for -teen and -ty.
Daily routines
get up · have breakfast · go to school · have lunch · do homework · have dinner · go to bed
Present simple
I get up at seven o'clock. · He gets up at six o'clock. (he/she/it + s)
Telling the time
It's seven o'clock. (7:00) · It's half past seven. (7:30)

glosari: Things you do every day at the same time.

nota.t: Present continuous
We use am / is / are + verb-ing for things happening now.
I am reading. · She is cooking. · They are playing.
Spelling: run → running · swim → swimming · write → writing · dance → dancing
Verb + ing
Months of the year
January · February · March · April · May · June · July · August · September · October · November · December
Ordinal numbers
1st first · 2nd second · 3rd third · 4th fourth · 5th fifth · 10th tenth · 12th twelfth
My birthday is in May. · It is on the 5th of May.

glosari: A number that shows order, like first, second, third.

nota.t: There is / There are

There is a sofa in the living room. · There are two beds in the bedroom.
Is there a garden? — Yes, there is. · Are there any chairs? — No, there aren't.
Prepositions of place
in · on · under · next to · behind · in front of · between · opposite
Things in a house
Countable and uncountable
We can count some food: an apple, two eggs. We cannot count others: some rice, some milk.
some / any
There is some milk. · There isn't any juice. · Is there any bread?
Polite requests

Would you like some tea? — Yes, please. / No, thank you.
Can I have a sandwich, please?
Food words

glosari: Things we can count, like apples and eggs.
Things we cannot count one by one, like rice, water and sugar.

nota.t: Places in town
school · hospital · library · park · market · mosque · bank · police station · post office · bus stop
Directions
Go straight. · Turn left. · Turn right. · It's next to the bank.
How do you go there?
I go to school by bus. · I go to the park on foot.
Places in town

glosari: Words that tell you how to get to a place.

nota.t: was / were
We use was and were to talk about the past.

I was at home yesterday. · They were at the zoo last Sunday.
Were you at school? — Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.

glosari: The time before now, like yesterday or last week.

nota.t: Past simple
For most verbs, add -ed: play → played, visit → visited, walk → walked.
Some verbs change: go → went · eat → ate · see → saw · have → had · buy → bought · swim → swam
We went to Langkawi last year. We swam in the sea.
Past tense verbs

glosari: The verb form for things that happened in the past.

nota.t: Comparing
short words: tall → taller → the tallest · big → bigger → the biggest
An elephant is bigger than a cat. · The giraffe is the tallest animal.
must / mustn't
We must keep the park clean. · We mustn't throw rubbish in the river.
Comparing words

glosari: To say how two things are different.
